title: Token content that is a number

source.note: composed: Table 1 calls a token's content "an opaque token interpreted by end-points" and does not fix its type. A number decodes, and validate reports a Warning of its own rather than the Error a non-string `text` content gets.

notes: Table 1 does not say a token's content is a string, Annex A allows `Content` any type, and §6.2's echo — "the exact same format, subformat and content" — is as well defined for a number as for a string: it can be compared and returned unchanged. A string is what the word token means everywhere it comes from, so the finding is reported; it is a Warning because the message is still interpretable, which is what that severity means here. `ecma430-5.1.4/text-content` stays an Error and stays `text`-only: natural language that is not a string has no reading at all.
